expectations.evidence: "### 1. Subscribe modal is an inescapable keyboard trap — WCAG: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (Level A)"; mechanics match the fixture exactly (Escape unhandled, no close control, Tab from #m-submit wraps to #m-email)
"### 2. Beach open/closed status is conveyed by color alone — WCAG: 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A)" at ul.status-list .dot / "Pillar Point, Half Moon Bay, Montara"

One widget-page defect claim falls outside the label — "Personal-data inputs missing `autocomplete` ... `widget.html:38` (email), `widget.html:40` (ZIP)" (1.3.5) — but it is verifiable in the fixture (both inputs genuinely lack autocomplete) and is a legitimate AA criterion, not an invention; counted in the false_positives metric per the matching rule. The two minor widget notes (modal background not inert; `list-style: none` stripping list semantics) assert no SC and are factually correct against widget.html:35 and :14. No decoys exist for this fixture.

All seven widget.html citations verified against the fixture: :35-64 = modal div through end of keydown handler; :26-30 = the status <ul>; :17-18 = `.open{background:#2e7d32}` / `.closed{background:#c62828}`; :38 = #m-email; :40 = #m-zip; :14 = `.status-list{list-style:none}`. Also independently checked the computed "5.13:1 and 5.62:1 on white" figures — both correct. Grounding is real, not invented (rubric override of the label's grounding_note).
